title.narrative: 1.4 # of WROs with increased L&A capacities.1.4.1 Areas in which WROs increased their L&A capacities as a result of CMI! Strategies, as reported by WROs.

description.narrative: This indicator measures the number of WROs with increased L&A capacities and show the specific areas of L&A capacities.

comment.narrative: The baseline indicator measures new values occurring at the start of the intervention, which has been set at 0.

This indicator is unique as the number of WROs with increased L&A will be reported only once. If different support is provided to the same WHRDs, they will be counted once, and details will be provided in the comment box.

CMI! contributed to the WROs' organizational strengthening and resilience by providing the required support to expand the organizations' skillset through the hiring of key staff and by facilitating, through endorsement letters and other ways, their resource mobilization efforts. In several instances, WROs were able to access additional core funding.

Core funding is provided to WROS to build resilient organisations. Results show that WROs used core funding by hiring and working with more staff and/or volunteers and/or by securing additional funding sources to support their missions.

All of the groups that are not anonymous reported doing both with the support they recevied from Mama Cash through CMI!

title.narrative: 1.5 # of strengthened and/or new alliances and 1.5.1 Type of alliance

description.narrative: This indicator measures the number of strengthened alliances and or new alliances created through CMI member interventions, and this includes listing the qualitative indicator of the type of alliance

comment.narrative: The baseline indicator measures new values occurring at the start of the intervention, which has been set at 0.

The reporting measure of this indicator is unique. New or strengthened alliances at different levels will be captured. In case one alliance is created in the first year, we shall only count for that year regardless of the number of times activities will be carried out to strengthen that alliance.

All of the mentioned alliances enhance Takatoat's reach. This includes a wider spread of feminist knowledge throughout Jordan and across the region through online and offline activism. Some alliances also allowed Takatoat to move into the area of sexual and reproductive health and rights to tackle a boader range of issues that women in Arabic-speaking region struggle with.The feminist oral history network which KW is a core part of opens possibilities for regional collaborations again in the MENA region, after this aspect of our work subsided with the pandemic and the political/economic situation in Lebanon. The network helps us support each other as we mainstream oral history as important tools for community building and transformation in attitudes, and in knowledge production.Power Up is a cohort of human rights based organizations situated in different parts of the world (UK, Africa, South Asia). This alliance has opened a new avenue for us to engage with organizations working in various geographical contexts. This is a huge opportunity for us to get in touch with human rights discourses and contexts beyond our national borders. Advance Multipurpose Co-operative Society Ltd is an association for headmasters and headmistresses of government schools in West Bengal. We have been in touch with this alliance since June this year for organising sensitization programs in schools. This alliance has helped us network with educators in West Bengal and further our sensitization programs in schools with teachers and students. Adding one more example the alliance with Revival disability has opened up newer possibilities in us in terms of understanding the connection between queerness, disability, consent, desire and agency.Through the alliance with LGBTIQA community/group, we got opportunity to internalize and practice the intersectionality in our work patterns. Similarly, the alliance with IT related organizations and companies has enabled us to advance our objective under our digital rights and accessibility project.Participation in other networks, campaigns and movements is important as it strengthens the work of the group, especially in strengthening grassroot demands, building collective strength, accessing specialized information, knowledge and training opportunities, and networking with government departments. Movements too are strengthened by the groups participation as the experience of grassroot women leaders and organizing adds women's perspective and knowledge to these movements. Single Women leaders have stood firm and have created a space for their equal and valued participation in many campaigns and mass events, challenging patriarchal mindsets. In this year our engagement with the food security campaign has been successful in opening the food security portal for addition of new families after a period of more than 2 years. The experience of widowed and other single women headed households and their desperation in the trying times of COVID added urgency to the need for the portal to be opened. The delay in the opening of the portal has meant that this has been a partial success only. The engagement with the National Coalition for Natural Farming has allowed the group to access training opportunities in sustainable agriculture for grassroot leaders and for back support staff. Often at events and trainings of this coalition the only women farmers present are from the group.

CMI! supported WROs to create and strengthen alliances at the national and regional level with other feminist and human rights organizations, networks and groups. These alliances have enabled WROs to decentralize their work by expanding its reach; monitor and provide support to their community members; mobilize legal experts; raise awareness; amplify the experiences of their constituencies in regional and national platforms and break their isolation; increase their visibility within and outside the feminist movement; and further deveop intersectional alliances.

The reporting measure of this indicator is unique. New or strengthened alliances at different levels will be captured. In case one alliance is created in the first year, we shall only count for that year regardless of the number of times activities will be carried out to strengthen that alliance.

Groups in Asia reported working in alliances in order to collaborate with other organisation that support and advance their mission. For example, to disseminate their advocacy messages around bodily autonomy to advance the politics and ethics of care for non-binary, trans people, and intersex people. Groups collaborated with service providing organisations that focus on LGBTI communities with psycho-social care, they hosted workshops and the publication of books with publishishers and writing collectives, to name just a couple of examples of how groups furthered the rights of their communities by working in alliances with other organisations.

Thanks to CMI!'s support, WROs were able to strengthen and expand their alliances to a wide range of actors among civil society, government, feminist movements and other social justice movements. These alliances have been opportunities for learning, networking, sharing experiences, joint strategizing, advocacy, and monitoring of women's rights. They have also widened the scope of the movement's action, and have provided spaces to give voice and visibility to historically excluded groups.

The reporting measure of this indicator is unique. New or strengthened alliances at different levels will be captured. In case one alliance is created in the first year, we shall only count for that year regardless of the number of times activities will be carried out to strengthen that alliance.

WROs build networks and alliances, both formal and informal, that create connections with other organisations and strengthen movements. In 2021, WROs supported by CMI! through Mama Cash have made these alliances more inclusive of issues that directly affect structurally excluded women and girls. These are people who face sex or gender discrimination such as non-binary, gender non-conforming, trans and intersex people.
